title: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense
line: Black attacks the center pawn at once, and the queens often come off early.

steps.text: The opening moves of the Ruy Lopez.
Bring the bishop out to attack the knight that guards the pawn on e5.
steps.after: This is the Berlin Defense: the other knight comes out and attacks your pawn on e4.

steps.text: Castle and let the pawn go. You will get it back.

also.d2d3: Guarding the pawn is the other main way, and keeps the queens on. This lesson castles.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It attacks the pawn on e5 and opens lines toward the black king.
steps.after: The knight steps back and attacks your bishop.

steps.text: Take the knight on c6. It removes a guard of the pawn on e5.

also.d4e5: Taking the pawn first is also played. This lesson takes the knight first.

steps.text: Take the pawn on e5. It also chases the knight.
Trade queens with check. Black's king has to take back and loses the right to castle.

also.d1e2: Keeping the queens is also played. This lesson trades them.

steps.after: The Berlin endgame. Black's king can no longer castle, but Black has the two bishops and no weak points.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. Your pawn on e5 gives you space, and on the king side you have four pawns to three.

also.h2h3: That is also played. This lesson brings the knight out.

steps.after: Black will try to free its bishops. You will try to use the extra pawn on the king side.

summary: Black wins the center pawn for a moment, gives it back, and trades queens for a solid endgame.
